biography:
Jorge Machado, born and raised in the vibrant heart of São Paulo, Brazil, discovered his love for speed not on the football field like many of his peers, but amidst the roaring engines and tire smoke of local karting tracks. His father, a mechanic with a passion for vintage Volkswagens, instilled in him a deep appreciation for the mechanics of racing. Jorge started competing in Copa Fusca, a grassroots racing series, where his raw talent and flashy style quickly gained him attention. He was known for pushing his Beetle to its absolute limit, often resulting in spectacular overtakes or equally spectacular crashes. This caught the eye of a Metalmoro MRX P4 team owner, providing him with a step up into prototype racing.

For several seasons, Machado shone in the MRX P4 series, showcasing flashes of brilliance that hinted at a potential future in international motorsport. However, inconsistency and a tendency to over-drive the car plagued his progress. Despite a few podium finishes and a reputation for exciting racing, he never quite managed to string together a championship-winning campaign. Now, at 34, Machado finds himself at a critical juncture in his career. The opportunities are fewer, the competition is fiercer, and the pressure to prove his worth is mounting. 

His recent performances have been underwhelming, leading many to question whether his best days are behind him. Sponsorship is becoming harder to secure, and younger drivers are hungry to take his place. Yet, Machado remains defiant, clinging to the belief that he still has what it takes to compete at the highest level. He has been working with a sports psychologist to control his temper, which sometimes surfaces during and after races, but whether this will translate to improved results on the track remains to be seen.

He still dreams of racing in Europe, and is trying to make connections with teams there. For now, he is trying to make a living driving the Metalmoro, and is teaching new drivers at local race schools.
drivingStyle: Machado is an aggressive, flamboyant driver known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks. He thrives in wheel-to-wheel combat, often pushing the limits of his car and his competitors. While his aggressive style can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also makes him prone to errors and costly crashes. He is not known for his tire management, preferring to push hard from the start, hoping to build a lead before his tires degrade. In high-pressure situations, Machado tends to become erratic, either pulling off a miraculous performance or making a critical mistake.

Costa is a rising star in the MRX P4 series, and Machado sees her as a direct threat to his position. He feels she has been given preferential treatment due to her family's connections, fueling his animosity.
Oliveira replaced Machado at a higher-tier team that he was trying to get into, leading to a personal conflict.

quirks: Always wears a specific pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, during race weekends.
Listens to a specific samba song on repeat for at least an hour before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to wash his helmet visor on race days, believing that the accumulated dirt and grime somehow improve his vision.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the smartest, it's about being the bravest. If you're afraid to push the limits, you're in the wrong business!"
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Interlagos MRX P4 race after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty. He made a series of daring overtakes in the rain to claim victory in front of his home crowd.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 Curitiba MRX P4 race, costing him a potential championship title. A reckless overtake attempt resulted in contact with a rival, sending both cars into the wall.
